metaTitle: Appliance Repair Marketing and Lead Flow You Own
metaDescription: Appliance repair marketing that builds your own lead flow: Local Services Ads, Business Profile, search ads and booked-job tracking. All in accounts you own.
intro: Appliance repair marketing builds a steady flow of calls for refrigerator, washer, dryer and oven repairs into accounts you own. We run your Local Services Ads, Business Profile, search ads and tracking, so each call is yours and can be traced to the job where your CRM supports it.

sections.heading: How appliance repair demand reaches you
paragraphs: BLS counted 6,354 private appliance repair and maintenance establishments in the US in 2025, employing 24,056 people, an average of fewer than four people per establishment. A separate BLS survey put home appliance repairer jobs at 32,150 in May 2025.

The work arrives one broken appliance at a time: a refrigerator that stopped cooling, a washer that won't drain. Refrigeration never takes a season off, and EIA lists it among the year-round home energy uses, along with water heating and lighting.

We build for high call volume at lower ticket sizes, so the marketing brings steady call volume and screens out work you can't take, like brands you don't service or addresses outside your drive time. Your own call and job history, not a generic calendar, tells us when to push.

sections.heading: How ASP builds appliance repair leads in your name
paragraphs: We build the channels that produce appliance repair leads in your name: your Local Services Ads account, your Google Business Profile, your search campaigns and your website. Every call and booking comes through accounts you control.
Instead of paying per lead for calls from a source you don't control, you're building a profile, reviews and pages that stay with your business.
bullets: Local Services Ads, where Google lists appliance repair services as an eligible category and you pay by the lead.
Your Google Business Profile, kept current with services, service areas, photos, posts and reviews.
Google Search Ads grouped by appliance and service, with a negative keyword list that filters out jobs you don't take.
Missed-call coverage: if you run Housecall Pro, ASP configures its CSR AI on the Growth tier to pick up missed calls and book appointments.

sections.heading: Local Services Ads for appliance repair
paragraphs: Google lists 'Appliance repair services' as a Local Services Ads category in the US. Its requirements for the category include business and owner checks for select users, general and professional liability insurance, and state-level business and owner licenses where local law calls for them.

Before ads can run, you need a public, verified Google Business Profile, and Google puts screening and verification at 3–4 weeks on average once your documents are submitted. The badge Google issues now is called Google Verified.

Where your ad shows depends on more than the bid. Google scores profile quality from your star rating, number of reviews, average response time, image quality and the checks you've passed, and missed calls can count against you. Leads can come in as calls, message requests or bookings, and appliance repair is on Google's list of home-service types its booking integrations support.

sections.heading: Show your EPA certification
paragraphs: Federal EPA rules under Clean Air Act Section 608 require certification for technicians who service equipment that could release refrigerant, and Type I certification covers small appliances. EPA's definition of small appliances includes home refrigerators and freezers, room and window air conditioners, dehumidifiers and under-the-counter ice makers sealed at the factory with five pounds of refrigerant or less.
If your techs hold that certification, it belongs on your refrigerator, freezer and ice maker pages and in your profile.

sections.heading: How results are measured
paragraphs: Each lead is tagged by where it came from, whether that is Local Services Ads, the map, a search ad or organic search. Where your CRM supports it, that tag follows the lead to the booked repair and its revenue. You see cost per booked job by channel, not just a pile of calls.
On Housecall Pro? Attribution setup comes with every Growth System tier. ASP is an Official Housecall Pro Affiliate Partner (discounts for new HCP accounts only).

sections.heading: What you own
paragraphs: Your Local Services Ads, Google Ads and Meta accounts are opened in your name, and you pay the platforms directly. Your Business Profile and reviews, your website and domain, and your customer and call data stay yours, with no exit fees if you leave.

faqs.question: Where do the appliance repair leads come from?
faqs.answer: From channels we build and run for your business, such as Local Services Ads, your Business Profile and search ads. Every lead comes into accounts in your name.

faqs.question: Can an appliance repair company run Local Services Ads?
faqs.answer: Yes, in the US where Google offers it in your area. Google lists appliance repair services as an eligible category. You'll need the insurance Google lists, state-level licenses where local law requires them, background checks if Google selects you, and a public, verified Business Profile.

faqs.question: Which appliances should get their own pages?
faqs.answer: We start with the repairs your customers search for most and what each booked job is worth to you, then look at what the competing pages offer. A repair with steady demand and good margin gets its own page first.

faqs.question: What do you need from us?
faqs.answer: Access to your own accounts, a clear answer on which appliances, brands and areas you want more of, and a plan for answering calls fast. Response time and reviews feed straight into how Local Services Ads rank.

faqs.question: How much does appliance repair marketing cost?
faqs.answer: Local SEO Pro is $1,200 a month on its own. The full Growth System is $2,500 a month for Foundation and $3,850 for Growth, which adds paid media management, and Premier is custom. Your ad spend goes to the platforms directly; see our pricing page for details.

faqs.question: Do I keep everything if I stop working with ASP?
faqs.answer: Yes. The accounts, profile, website and data are in your name from day one, and there are no exit fees. Our What You Own page has the full list.
